A comprehensive theoretical framework has been developed to predict the spectral characteristics of magnetic impurities located on the surface of a superconducting material. This material-specific model focuses on the Yu--Shiba--Rusinov (YSR) states and incorporates spin-orbit coupling, enabling a first principles analysis of Mn atoms and their pairs on the Nb(110) surface using the GW+SOMF method. This approach combines Green's function many-body theory with a sophisticated electronic structure method that accounts for local spin polarization. The calculated results accurately depict the YSR state energies for isolated Mn adatoms and (100)-aligned Mn dimers on the Nb(110) surface, and also predict the YSR state configurations for various (n00)-aligned Mn dimer pairs. Spectral function calculations that incorporate the Bardeen formalism for tunneling current simulations on the Nb(110) surface further reveal the YSR state energy positions and spin orientations, showing strong agreement with experimental data for isolated Mn adatoms. Additionally, theoretical predictions for the spin orientation of YSR states in (100)-aligned Mn dimers on the Nb(110) surface are provided.
This report details an approach that leverages a convolutional neural network (CNN) for skin cancer detection, with a specific focus on managing highly imbalanced datasets.

Due to the tendency for high-energy lepton colliders to radiate forward, the remaining energy of the particles decreases, resulting in low collision rates at large center-of-mass energies. To address this issue, we re-examine the application of the effective vector boson approximation (EWVWA) to future muon colliders, taking into account all leading-order processes for particle-pair production at such energies, similar to what's done with electron colliders. In contrast to previous studies that considered only specific particle-pair production examples within the EWVWA framework, we present a more comprehensive set of predictions for EWVWA-based muon colliders. Additionally, we design an EWVWA-valid collision energy range for effective future muon collider designs. When compared to full-order calculations, the EWVWA provides accurate results at near-central production angles, whereas deviations occur at large rapidity angles similar to observed patterns in electron colliders. The EWVWA's accuracy improves with higher collision energies, and we suggest possible effective energy peaks for EWVWA-valid muon colliders, comparable to the EWVWA-based EWVWA valid PEpP and PPpP colliders.

In 1931, G\"odel's incompleteness theorem initially aimed to demonstrate that any consistent formal system extending basic arithmetic has an unprovable sentence within its framework. Following its publication, the theorem was frequently rephrased to highlight its diagonalization technique rather than its consistency argument. In 1933, Tarski's truth definition for arithmetic emerged, which is often seen as an extension of G\"odel's work, although it actually relies on the original proof's consistency argument. Subsequently, in 1942, Carnap's truth predicate was proposed for logical languages, which is also commonly viewed as related to G\"odel's theorem, but is actually grounded in the same consistency argument. Although the works of G\"odel, Tarski, Carnap are often linked, this connection is arguably inaccurate. In 1936, Rosser's strengthened incompleteness theorem actually established the foundation for these reformulations, which is often overlooked in discussions of G\"odel's work. Recentering the dialogue on G\"odel's original proof reveals that the sentence defined in G\"odel (1931) is actually the truth predicate for basic arithmetic as described by (G\"odel 1934a), which is also the self-referential sentence in (G\"odel 1934b) and not merely a special case of self-reference as commonly presented.

This article examines the concept of invariant manifolds in dynamical systems, particularly in the context of fractional-order linear systems described by a set of equations. A technique is presented to determine the stability of a fractional-order linear system by analyzing the distribution of eigenvalues in the complex plane. It is shown that an equation defined based on the fractional order does not leave an invariant curve in the system's parameter space, as illustrated through a specific example. Consequently, a fractional-order system is demonstrated that does not have an invariant manifold corresponding to one of its equations.

This research focuses on resolving an inverse problem where we aim to determine a source term within a structural acoustic partial differential equation (PDE) model. This model describes the interaction between a structural vibration and an acoustic wave. Uniqueness in solving this problem is established through a Carleman estimate, which incorporates a boundary observability condition. This condition involves measuring the acoustic wave's energy on a specific portion of the boundary. Additionally, a stability estimate of logarithmic type is also proven. A key aspect of this research is its ability to handle less regular solutions, allowing the source term to be determined solely from the oscillation's behavior on a part of the boundary.

Within the simplest scoto-seesaw model, we examine the consistency between the fermion mass mechanisms, evaluate the phenomenology of the extended Higgs sector, and analyze the scoto-seesaw parameter space. Here, a simple $U(1)_\\nu$ extended symmetry is implemented, allowing for the generation of neutron masses through the type-I and type-II seesaw mechanisms, as well as the possibility of breaking the electroweak symmetry through the vacuum expectation value of an additional singlet scalar. We propose a minimal extension of the model that includes an additional complex scalar doublet, enabling complex coupling constants and a potential for CPM violation. We analyze the decay of heavy neutral scalars into $WW$, $ZZ$, and $\\gamma\\gamma$ pairs, as well as the possibility of one of the scalar doublet components being a dark matter candidate. We also examine the possibility of dark matter self-interactions through scalar mediators and evaluate the parameter space for viable neutrino oscillation mixing angles. Furthermore, we extend the simplest scoto-seesaw model to include an additional dark doublet, and in a dark-doublet extended version, we analyze the potential for generating a neutrinoless double beta decay signal.
